html:
The Anglo-Irish Treaty, signed in London on 6 December 1921, ended the War of Independence and created the Irish Free State, a self-governing dominion of the British Empire.

The Free State covered 26 of Ireland's 32 counties. Northern Ireland, with its Protestant majority descended from the Plantation of Ulster, had already been given its own parliament and stayed in the United Kingdom. Irish members of parliament had to swear an oath of loyalty to the king.

Michael Collins, who signed it, said it gave the freedom to win freedom. Its opponents, led by Éamon de Valera, saw it as betraying the republic. The Dáil approved it narrowly, and the split led to the Irish Civil War. Collins said he had signed his own death warrant. See Ireland.
sum: The Anglo-Irish Treaty, signed in London on 6 December 1921, ended the War of Independence and created the Irish Free State, a self-governing dominion of the British Empire.
